answer: Sybil resistance can come from bonded stake: each agent locks collateral that glows like an ember while it does honest work and dims if abandoned. Every action carries a signed pulse, a small proof of liveness that random peers verify against costly real activity. When fake identities are exposed, their whole stake is slashed and burned, so spawning a swarm of bots becomes ruinously expensive instead of nearly free. Reputation builds like shale, in slow layers of verified history that cannot be forged cheaply, making honest behavior the cheapest strategy across the whole agent economy.
